releases.name: oc-metricboard v0.1.25
releases.body:
## oc-metricboard v0.1.25

Makes the plugin show its **version in opencode's `/plugins` panel**, matching oh-my-opencode-slim.

### Why it was missing

The panel renders a version only for **Server** entries whose source is a package with a version, and the version is attached only when that server entrypoint loads successfully. This package declared only `./tui`, so the server fell back to the root `"."` export — the TUI bundle, which imports `@opentui/solid` and cannot load in the server process. The load failed, so no version was ever attached.

### Fix

- Add `src/server.ts`: a dependency-free no-op server plugin (`{ id, setup }`), built to `dist/server.js` (170 bytes, imports nothing)
- Add `"./server": { "import": "./dist/server.js" }` to `exports`; the build now emits both `dist/tui.js` and `dist/server.js`

The plugins panel will show `oc-metricboard  0.1.25` on the Server row after restart.

**Tarball**: `oc-metricboard-0.1.25.tgz` (identical to the npm published content)

releases.name: oc-metricboard v0.1.19
releases.body:
## oc-metricboard v0.1.19

Dual-host support for opencode V1 (1.18.x) and V2 (2.0.x), plus TPS accuracy fixes. Upgrade recommended for V2 users.

### V2 support (0.1.12–0.1.16)

- **Dual-host module**: `./tui` exports both `{ id, tui }` (V1) and `{ id, setup }` (V2); each host reads its key and ignores the other
- **Ship built output**: `exports` (`.`/`./tui`) and `main` point at `./dist/tui.js` (tsc ESM + react-jsx). The V2 host resolves UI externals for built output only; raw `.tsx` gets sandbox-only resolution (`Cannot find package '@opentui/solid'`)
- **UI runtime alignment**: `@opentui/*@0.5.11` + `solid-js` as version-matched hard dependencies so the host prunes them from the sandbox and resolves host-side (fixes the `OPENTUI_FORCE_WCWIDTH` double-registration load failure)
- **V2 event bridge**: `session.text/reasoning.delta`, `step.started/ended`, `session.idle` forwarded as-is (field-compatible payloads); `execution.started` → `session.status(busy)`; `execution.succeeded/failed/interrupted` → `session.idle` fallback. Sub-agent attribution via `ctx.data.session.root/family`
- Server-side `setup` probe (no `ctx.ui`) exits silently instead of throwing

### TPS accuracy (0.1.17–0.1.19)

- **Idle TPS freeze**: an open-but-silent request ends its window at `lastDeltaTime` instead of `now`, so the reading freezes instead of decaying in real time while idle
- **Host-time stamping**: all handler timestamps prefer the V2 envelope's host `created` stamp (V1 unchanged — no `created` there). Measures generation time, not flush-arrival time
- **Turn-anchored fallback with tool subtraction**: per-delta times may still be delivery-stamped (batched flushes), so when the per-step window implies a physically impossible rate (> 300 t/s), TPS falls back to `(turn end − turn start − tool overlap)` forestep tokens. Per-turn tool spans are tracked from `tool.called/success/failed` (unioned for parallel calls). Behavior is bit-identical whenever the per-step window is credible

**Tarball**: `oc-metricboard-0.1.19.tgz` (identical to the npm published content)

releases.name: oc-metricboard v0.1.11
releases.body:
## oc-metricboard v0.1.11

### Fixed

- **Session elapsed no longer grows unboundedly**: after reopening a session, the Session readout (accumulated busy time) kept growing in real time while idle and could reach tens of hours (62.3h observed). Two stacked defects:
  1. During hydration the session-status lookup resolves to an empty string on the current host SDK dialect, so every hydrated session kept an open active interval anchored to its last user message - counting all post-message wall-clock time (idle included) as active
  2. `toPerformanceTime` maps pre-process wall times to negative performance timestamps; the open interval became `{start: -62h, end: now}`, so its span included the entire era before the TUI process existed

  Hydration now closes all intervals from history and always returns `activeSince = null`. Activity accounting resumes exclusively via live busy/idle events; historical busy spans (user message ? assistant completed) are still accumulated correctly
- Diagnostics: added a `timing hydrate` summary line (elapsed / activeSince / interval stats) for troubleshooting timing issues

releases.name: oc-metricboard v0.1.10
releases.body:
## oc-metricboard v0.1.10

Fixes several metric display issues accumulated since v0.1.5 (upgrade recommended).

### TTFT fixes

- **TTFT no longer inflates with turn duration**: every intra-turn step request inherited the turn's original start time, so TTFT in long agentic sessions grew to the full turn runtime (e.g. 11m54s). Only un-streamed placeholder requests inherit the anchor now (#2cbab96)
- **Turn-level TTFT**: anchored to "user message -> first token of the turn", stable across all steps and tool executions within a turn, refreshed on each new turn (#1bcd035)
- **Model rows consistent with the main aggregate**: they use the same turn-level TTFT and no longer show 0ms (#a0ae05b)
- TTFT beyond 10 minutes renders as `--`

### Hydration fixes (state restore on session reopen)

- **Hydration had been failing silently ever since the plugin existed**: the host client speaks a flat-key SDK dialect (`{ sessionID }` / `{ id }`); nested shapes left a literal `{sessionID}` template in the URL, the server rejected every hydration request, and the failure surfaced only in `response.error`. Shapes now try the runtime-verified flat form first with nested fallbacks (#81a367d, #87c2b3f, #69961cb)
- **Historical tokens restore immediately on reopen** (including sub-agent sessions)

### Stale model rows

- Model breakdown rows now respect foreground-turn membership: a model switched away from hours ago no longer lingers with frozen token counts (#283a6f8)
- Hydrated turns complete based on the last assistant message's completed flag, so old sub-agent sessions no longer stay "open" forever (#f063ebd)

### UI

- Fixed the header arrow not updating when collapsing/expanding MetricBoard (#ef57c59)

### Other

- Added the missing `modelBreakdown` field to `aggregateRequestMetrics`
